questions.question: Running `dbt seed && dbt run` against `extras/sample_dbt_project` with the seed data unmodified, how many rows should `stg_customers` produce, and why?
options: 20 rows, because all seeded customers pass through unfiltered
18 rows, because 2 of the 20 seeded customers (ids 106 and 115) have is_active = false and are filtered out
25 rows, because stg_customers includes orders too
0 rows, because dbt seed does not load CSVs automatically
questions.explanation: stg_customers.sql filters WHERE is_active = true. Of the 20 seeded customers, ids 106 and 115 have is_active = false, leaving 18 rows — the same number referenced throughout Day 84B and Day 84C as 'the 18 active customers.'

questions.question: Why does `int_order_items.sql` use `materialized='ephemeral'` instead of `view` or `table`?
options: Ephemeral models are required for any model using a WHERE clause
Ephemeral models compile inline as a CTE in downstream models with no separate database object — appropriate for intermediate logic that nothing outside dbt needs to query directly
Ephemeral models are the fastest materialization for marts that BI tools query directly
Ephemeral is a synonym for incremental
questions.explanation: Ephemeral models don't persist as a view or table in the warehouse; dbt inlines their SQL as a CTE wherever they're ref()'d. This fits int_order_items, which exists purely to be consumed by fct_revenue — no BI tool or analyst queries it directly.

questions.question: A teammate sets `loaded_at_field: sign_up_date` for a freshness check, where `sign_up_date` is stored as a DATE column. What happens, and how was this fixed in `extras/sample_dbt_project/models/staging/sources.yml`?
options: Nothing — DATE and TIMESTAMP are interchangeable in dbt freshness checks
dbt source freshness errors with a type mismatch; the fix was to set loaded_at_field to a cast expression: "CAST(sign_up_date AS TIMESTAMP)"
dbt automatically casts DATE to TIMESTAMP with no configuration needed
The freshness check silently always passes when given a DATE column
questions.explanation: dbt's freshness check expects loaded_at_field to resolve to a TIMESTAMP. A DATE column causes a database error. The documented fix in sources.yml is loaded_at_field: "CAST(sign_up_date AS TIMESTAMP)" — described in the lesson as 'a real, common dbt freshness bug.'

questions.question: You intentionally set one order's amount_cents to a negative number in the seed data and rerun `dbt seed && dbt run && dbt test`. What does the resulting dbt_utils.accepted_range test failure report, and what does it NOT show you by default?
options: It shows the exact bad row's order_id; you don't need to query further
It reports a result count like 'Got 1 result, configured to fail if != 0' but does not show you the offending row — you must query the model directly to find it
It automatically fixes the negative value and reruns
It silently passes because accepted_range only checks upper bounds
questions.explanation: dbt test failures report a count ('Got 1 result, configured to fail if != 0'), not the offending rows. Triaging a real failure requires a manual query like SELECT * FROM fct_revenue WHERE amount_usd < 0 — exactly the workflow Exercise 3 has you practice.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a dbt 'contract' and a dbt 'test'?
options: They are the same feature with two names
A contract pins column names/types and fails the run at compile/build time if violated; a test checks data values/quality and fails at dbt test time
Contracts only apply to seeds, never to models
Tests are deprecated in favor of contracts
questions.explanation: A contract (config: contract: enforced: true) guarantees structural stability — column names and types — and fails loudly if a model change violates it. Tests (not_null, unique, accepted_range, etc.) check the values within that structure are valid data.

questions.question: What problem does 'Slim CI' (--select state:modified+ combined with --defer) solve?
options: It makes dbt tests run without a database connection
It rebuilds the entire 500-model project on every CI run for safety
It rebuilds only models changed in a PR and their downstream dependents, deferring unchanged upstream models to production state, instead of rebuilding the whole DAG from raw sources every time
It replaces the need for any tests in CI
questions.explanation: Slim CI compares a PR's manifest against the last successful prod manifest (--state) to select only modified models and downstream dependents, and defers unchanged upstream models to prod rather than rebuilding them in CI — keeping CI fast on large projects.

questions.question: An incremental model filters `WHERE created_at > (SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM {{ this }})` with no unique_key set. What production risk does this introduce?
options: No risk — this is the recommended pattern for all incremental models
Late-arriving or updated rows with an older timestamp than the last run's max will be silently missed, and without a unique_key, any reprocessed row would be duplicated rather than updated
The model will fail to compile
This pattern only works with ephemeral materializations
questions.explanation: Filtering only on MAX(timestamp) misses late-arriving or backfilled rows older than the current max. Without a unique_key, dbt has no way to update an existing row in place, so reprocessing produces duplicates. Both are named pitfalls in this lesson's Production Workflow section.

questions.question: Why might `--full-refresh` be dangerous to run automatically in a CI/CD pipeline against a production incremental model?
options: It is always instant and free, so there's no real risk
It rebuilds the entire incremental model from scratch, which can be a multi-hour, expensive operation on a multi-billion-row table if triggered accidentally
It only affects ephemeral models, not incremental ones
It is required after every single dbt run
questions.explanation: --full-refresh discards incremental state and rebuilds the whole table from raw history. On a large production table this can be slow and costly (recall Phase 7 Day 83's bytes-scanned economics), so the lesson recommends gating it behind manual approval rather than an automatic CI flag.
